headline: CISA adds actively exploited N-able MailAssure and MONAI Label flaws to KEV catalog
summary: CISA added two vulnerabilities to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog, citing active exploitation. One is CVE-2026-134624 (CVSS 9.3), a server-side request forgery flaw tied to LDAP in N-able MailAssure. The other is a MONAI Label zero-day that reporting links to AI-agent-driven exploitation; its CVE ID was not available in the source excerpt.

headline: Peninsula Energy halts trading after cyber incident at Wyoming uranium project
summary: Peninsula Energy told the ASX that a cybersecurity incident at its Wyoming uranium project will temporarily affect operations. It has halted trading in its shares. The cause and scope have not been disclosed.

headline: CISA orders federal patching of exploited N-able email security flaw by Thanksgiving
summary: CISA has warned that a vulnerability in an N-able email security platform is being actively exploited. It gave government departments until Thanksgiving to patch it. Separately, N-able is restoring the email platform.

summary: Microsoft warned that attackers exploited a vulnerability in Azure API Management Classic tiers to steal API credentials stored by customers. Norwegian authorities linked the flaw to cyberattacks on energy companies. Sources do not give a CVE or full technical details.

summary: Norway's NSM says an Azure API Management Classic vulnerability affected several Norwegian businesses, including Equinor and Skagerak Energi. summary: Socket researchers found 13 malicious NuGet packages tied to fake developer job assessments. The packages use DLL side-loading, steal credentials and rely on GitHub-hosted malware infrastructure.

headline: European Commission confirms user data stolen in EU Academy platform breach
summary: The European Commission confirmed that attackers breached its EU Academy online learning platform. Personal data belonging to an undisclosed number of users was stolen.

headline: European Commission finds EU Academy user data exposed in October cyberattack
summary: The European Commission's investigation into a cyberattack it detected in October found that names and email addresses of EU Academy users were exposed. The source describes the attack as AI-assisted. It does not give the number of affected users.

headline: Broadcom patches 23 VMware flaws, including critical vCenter vmdir auth bypass CVE-2026-123903
summary: Broadcom fixed 23 vulnerabilities across VMware ESX, vCenter, Workstation, Fusion and Avi Load Balancer. The most serious, CVE-2026-123903 (CVSS 9.8), is an authentication bypass in the VMware Directory Service (vmdir). The source does not report active exploitation of this new flaw, though it follows an earlier vCenter zero-day.

headline: CISA reports active exploitation of hardcoded credentials in Cisco Expressway
summary: CISA reports that attackers are actively exploiting hardcoded credentials in Cisco Expressway, which is used for enterprise collaboration and video gateways. The short source report gives no details on the CVE, affected versions or victims.
overrides: No source-reported exploitation or recent KEV evidence; vulnerability capped at high

headline: VMware patches critical ESX code-execution and vCenter authentication-bypass flaws
summary: VMware has released updates fixing critical vulnerabilities, including an authentication bypass in vCenter and flaws that could allow code execution on ESX hosts. The source does not report any exploitation in the wild.

headline: AI-enabled campaign exploits critical flaws in Check Point Security Management servers
summary: A campaign described as AI-enabled has exploited critical vulnerabilities in Check Point Security Management servers. At least 22 organizations were compromised. The source does not name the CVEs, the actors or the affected sectors.
overrides: No source-reported exploitation or recent KEV evidence; vulnerability capped at high

headline: Attackers exploit vulnerabilities to compromise Check Point management servers at 22 organizations
summary: An ongoing campaign has used multiple vulnerabilities to compromise Check Point Security management servers at 22 organizations. The source does not name the vulnerabilities, the affected sectors or the victims' locations. Because these servers control firewall policy, a compromise could weaken network defenses.

headline: VMware warns of multiple critical vulnerabilities that could give attackers system access
summary: VMware has disclosed several critical vulnerabilities across multiple products that could give attackers access to systems. The source does not name the products or CVEs, and it does not report any exploitation.

headline: Check Point Security Management servers compromised in AI-assisted campaign across sectors
summary: Attackers reportedly compromised Check Point Security Management servers in a campaign the report describes as AI-assisted. The attacks came from 99 IP addresses and hit organizations in several industries and countries. The source does not name a CVE or a threat actor.

headline: Critical flaw lets attackers remotely take over Danfoss refrigeration systems
summary: A critical vulnerability lets attackers take remote control of Danfoss refrigeration systems. A security update has been released. The source reports no active exploitation.

headline: KEPCO confirms network breach exposing data of about 1.5 million people
summary: Korea Electric Power Corporation confirmed that a threat actor got into its internal network and accessed two systems. Those systems held data on customers, employees and contractors, affecting about 1.5 million people.

headline: Okta links ShinyHunters-associated vishing cluster O-UNC-053 to new INCEPTION data leak site
summary: Okta Threat Intelligence assesses that O-UNC-053, a voice-phishing cluster previously linked to ShinyHunters, may have rebranded as INCEPTION and launched a new data leak site. The group calls targets to get them to enter credentials on phishing pages and approve authentication prompts. Okta presents the rebrand as a possibility, not a confirmed fact.

headline: Unauthenticated SQL injection in WHMCS shopping cart can expose customer data and admin hashes
summary: WHMCS, a billing and automation platform used by many web hosting providers, disclosed a SQL injection in its shopping cart. An unauthenticated attacker could use it to pull customer records and administrator password hashes. Two other flaws that need a client login were disclosed at the same time, and the vendor has released fixes. No exploitation has been reported.

headline: Critical unauthenticated buffer overflow in Danfoss AK-SM 8xxA controllers awaits vendor fix
summary: CISA advisory ICSA-26-328-03 describes CVE-2026-129713 (CVSS 9.8), a stack-based overflow in an unauthenticated CGI handler on Danfoss AK-SM 8xxA controllers up to version 5.4.0. Crafted POST requests can crash the webserver, and the advisory says code execution is possible in theory. A fix is planned for version 5.5.x. The advisory does not report any exploitation.

headline: New 'Inception' extortion brand linked to SSO voice-phishing campaign
summary: Okta and ReversingLabs linked a new extortion brand called Inception to a voice-phishing campaign targeting employees' single sign-on credentials. The source does not say which sectors or regions are targeted.

headline: KEPCO breach exposes personal data of 1.5 million people
summary: Hackers stole personal information from the customer portal and supplier relationship management platform of South Korea's state electric utility, KEPCO. About 1.5 million people are reported to be affected.

headline: Okta: ShinyHunters-linked crew O-UNC-053 resurfaces on new 'Inception' leak site
summary: Okta threat intelligence reports that O-UNC-053, a crew that supplied victims to the ShinyHunters leak site, appears to have moved to a new leak site called 'Inception'. The ShinyHunters site went offline in September. Since March 2026 the cluster has run social engineering and credential-harvesting campaigns against many sectors, including technology, financial services, insurance, retail and transportation.

headline: WordPress.org blocks backdoored updates in six WP connect plugins
summary: WordPress.org blocked backdoors in six plugins from the vendor WP connect. This reportedly stopped the malware from reaching thousands of sites. The source does not give full details on when the backdoors were inserted or how many sites may already have received them.

headline: FCA warns UK financial firms to govern AI agent risks or face supervisory action
summary: The UK Financial Conduct Authority (FCA) said financial firms must maintain effective oversight and governance controls over AI agents as their use grows across the sector. The source frames this as a warning that firms which fail to address the risks may face action.

headline: Project Zero shows .NET loading quirk bypassing Windows code integrity and VirtualBox hardening
summary: A Google Project Zero researcher described how a .NET Framework file-loading behaviour lets a local attacker run untrusted code past Windows code integrity. The same behaviour also bypassed Oracle VirtualBox process hardening on Windows hosts, tracked as CVE-2026-87268. The source does not report any exploitation in the wild.

headline: Industrial serial gateways openly advertise missing authentication
summary: Researchers found that many industrial serial-to-Ethernet gateways reveal whether authentication is enabled, and many have none. That exposes critical OT access devices to discovery and misuse.

headline: OpenRouter removes three AI providers for data-handling violations that exposed prompts and secrets
summary: OpenRouter removed three AI model providers after finding they broke their stated data-handling policies and exposed sensitive data, including prompts and secrets. Customers who sent sensitive content through these providers may be affected.

headline: Ox Security reports AI agents can be manipulated through instruction files without malware
summary: Ox Security researchers describe an attack path in which AI agents are steered by tampered agent instructions instead of executable malware. The source gives no reported in-the-wild exploitation and no technical specifics.

headline: AutomationDirect C-More EA9 programming software heap overflow fixed in V6.81
summary: CISA advisory ICSA-26-328-01 covers CVE-2026-127280 (CVSS 7.8), a heap buffer overrun in C-More EA9 Programming Software V6.80 and earlier. Opening a malicious project file could corrupt memory and may allow code execution. Version 6.81 fixes the flaw.

headline: GAO finds USDA and FDA falling short on food sector cyber protection
summary: A US GAO report says federal agencies are missing opportunities to help protect the food and agriculture sector from cyber threats. USDA and FDA told GAO they lack the resources and staff to meet all of their infrastructure protection responsibilities.

headline: UK NCSC reports marked rise in AI-assisted cyberattacks since September
summary: The UK National Cyber Security Centre (NCSC) said it has seen a marked rise in AI-assisted cyberattacks since September. It warned that AI is increasing attackers' speed, scale and persistence. The source names no specific campaigns or victims.

headline: Anthropic expands enterprise safeguards for detecting Claude misuse
summary: Anthropic launched EFS for zero-retention enterprise customers. It helps them detect Claude misuse that is spread across many requests. Conversation data stays in the customer's own cloud.

headline: China-aligned Webworm suspected of using modified SoftEther VPN Bridge for covert remote access
summary: Researchers suspect that the China-aligned group Webworm is running a customised build of the open-source SoftEther VPN Bridge. The build appears to have known detection fingerprints removed, and it is disguised as network-monitoring software. It reportedly uses several tricks to hide from security tools while keeping covert access to compromised networks.

headline: Mozilla Firefox update fixes over 100 security vulnerabilities and adds per-site VPN option
summary: Mozilla has released a new Firefox version that fixes more than one hundred security vulnerabilities. The release also adds a VPN option that can be set per website. The source does not report any of these flaws being exploited.

headline: Elastic Security 9.6 adds AI agents for alert triage, Linux ransomware protection and LLM detection rules
summary: Elastic released Elastic Security 9.6 with AlertZero, a set of AI agents that triage alerts, hunt threats and tune detection rules. The release also adds ransomware protection for Linux, expanded entity resolution and 143 detection rules covering AI agent and LLM platforms.

headline: Unit 42 tracks attackers using autonomous AI agents for multi-platform intrusions
summary: Unit 42 describes campaigns in which attackers used autonomous AI agents to automate intrusions across multiple platforms. The agents used standard tools but left distinct operational traces.

headline: Virginia and Oregon file lawsuits against SpaceX over Grok-generated abuse imagery
summary: Two US states, Virginia and Oregon, have sued SpaceX over child sexual abuse material created with the Grok AI model. The suits say weak safeguards against nudification were part of the business strategy used to set Grok apart from rival models.

headline: OpenAI and Cisco release open-source Shirudo tool for temporary Linux exploit protection
summary: OpenAI and Cisco released Shirudo, an open-source AI-assisted tool for Linux. It applies temporary runtime protections to block exploitation of known vulnerabilities while administrators prepare patches. Services do not need to be restarted.

headline: Anthropic launches Claude Ship beta for agent-driven code review and approval
summary: Anthropic has released Claude Ship in beta. It is a set of agents that review pull requests, fix issues and approve changes within limits set by team policy. Teams control where it runs and which changes still need human approval.

headline: Amazon reports attackers used AI agents to find and exploit a zero-day with little human input
summary: Amazon says attackers used AI agents built on the Cairn AI framework to find and exploit a zero-day vulnerability with little human involvement. The source summary does not name the affected product, the victims or the actors.

headline: Schneider Electric EcoStruxure Power Build Rapsody use-after-free via malicious SSD files
summary: CISA advisory ICSA-26-328-02 (version 2) covers CVE-2026-119055, a medium-severity use-after-free flaw in EcoStruxure Power Build Rapsody, a switchboard design tool. A user would have to open a crafted SSD file, which could lead to code execution. Multiple regional editions are affected.

headline: ShinyHunters claims return on new leak site after FBI arrests, citing old PGP keys as proof
summary: The ShinyHunters extortion group claims to have returned through a new data leak site, following two months of arrests of alleged members. It cites old PGP keys as proof of identity. The claim has not been independently verified.

headline: Critical Bluetooth flaws reportedly expose trailer and caravan brake systems to attackers
summary: Researchers say they found several critical Bluetooth vulnerabilities that could let attackers reach the brake systems of trailers and caravans. The sources do not name the affected vendor, give CVEs, or report any exploitation in the wild.

headline: Kosovo suspect indicted for payment card theft is extradited to the US
summary: Kosovo has extradited Hektor Avdyli to the United States, where he faces an indictment for credit card theft. US authorities say a hard drive he held contained millions of payment card numbers.

headline: Carnegie Endowment donor data exposed in breach at vendor Soapbox Engage
summary: The Carnegie Endowment for International Peace says some donor information was leaked. The leak came from a cyberattack on its third-party vendor, Soapbox Engage. The source does not give the scope of the exposure.

headline: LaLiga confirms cyberattack exposed fans' personal data across league and club digital services
summary: Spain's professional football league LaLiga says a cyberattack on its digital services, and on those of several Spanish clubs, led to the theft of fans' personal data. The source does not give the attack method, the number of records or the threat actor.

headline: AI-agent driven attacks reported mainly exploiting low-hanging fruit such as exposed credentials
summary: A report covered by Security.NL says attacks carried out with AI agents and AI frameworks mostly exploit easy weaknesses, such as credentials left in public places. The source summary gives few further details.

headline: OpenAI and Cisco release Shirudo, an open-source tool to shield unpatched Linux systems
summary: OpenAI and Cisco have released Shirudo, an open-source tool. It uses AI-generated shields to block exploitation of known vulnerabilities on live Linux systems until patches are applied, without a restart. The vendors say it is not yet production-ready.

headline: GlobeTopper gift card platform breach exposes customer API credentials, about $70,000 redeemed
summary: iQSTEL disclosed in an SEC filing that its subsidiary GlobeTopper, a B2B gift card and top-up platform, was breached. Attackers stole some business customers' API credentials and redeemed about $70,000 in gift cards without authorization. The intrusion was detected on October 22, and the platform was taken offline. The company estimates lost revenue of up to $2.5 million.

headline: Bluetooth flaws in Elecbrakes trailer brake controllers allow forced braking
summary: Critical Bluetooth vulnerabilities in Elecbrakes trailer brake controllers could let a nearby attacker force a trailer to brake, which could cause accidents. The source does not report any exploitation.

headline: LaLiga discloses breach of football fans' personal data
summary: Spain's football league LaLiga says a breach exposed fans' personally identifiable information. The source does not say how many people were affected or how the attackers got in.

headline: LaLiga reports breach exposing personal data of users and some affiliated clubs
summary: LaLiga, Spain's top men's football league, has disclosed a breach in which attackers took personal information about users of its services. Users of some affiliated clubs' services were also affected. The source does not say how many people are affected or how the breach happened.

headline: McDonald's Japan discloses app database breach exposing customer location data
summary: McDonald's Japan disclosed that attackers accessed a database holding sensitive information on users of its official smartphone app. The exposed data includes customer location information. The source summary does not give the number of affected users.

headline: McDonald's Japan discloses breach exposing customer purchase and location data
summary: McDonald's Japan disclosed a cybersecurity breach that exposed customers' purchase histories and mobile device location data. The source does not give the number of people affected or the attack method.

headline: Qilin ransomware group claims breach of market research firm Ipsos
summary: The Qilin ransomware group claims it hacked market research firm Ipsos and stole files. Ipsos has not confirmed the claim in the source report.

headline: GlobeTopper cyberattack causes estimated $2.5M revenue loss and $70K gift card theft
summary: A cyberattack disrupted operations at GlobeTopper, a B2B top-up solutions provider, causing an estimated $2.5 million in lost revenue. The attacker redeemed digital gift cards worth about $70,000.

headline: Rabobank customer denied refund for unauthorized payments made with stolen phone
summary: A Rabobank customer will not be reimbursed for unauthorized payment transactions carried out with his stolen phone. The case concerns liability for mobile banking fraud in the Netherlands. The source gives few details about how the decision was reached.

headline: Kirsten Davies named Acting US National Cyber Director
summary: The US president named Kirsten Davies as Acting National Cyber Director, a pick that brings more industry experience to the role. The appointment follows recent outages and comes amid rising geopolitical tensions.

headline: Kirsten Davies to be nominated as US national cyber director; Jay Clayton named acting director
summary: Kirsten Davies is set to be nominated to succeed Sean Cairncross as US national cyber director, after a brief stint as acting director. Jay Clayton will take on the acting director role in addition to his current duties.

headline: Astelia launches autonomous network-level mitigation for reachable vulnerabilities
summary: Astelia has announced a feature that blocks network attack paths to vulnerabilities that attackers can reach, so organizations can mitigate them before a patch is available. The vendor presents it as a response to faster AI-driven exploitation.

headline: Op-ed: basic OT security gaps are more urgent than the post-quantum threat
summary: This opinion piece argues that post-quantum cryptography belongs on the roadmap. It also says that operational technology environments face more basic and more urgent threats today. The source names no specific incidents or vulnerabilities.

headline: Bedrock Data adds intent-aware runtime DLP for AI agents
summary: Bedrock Data says its Agent DLP product now infers the business purpose behind a user's task. It then checks the agent's combined tool and LLM actions against that purpose and the organization's policy. The update also adds support for off-the-shelf agents.

headline: CrowdStrike reportedly to acquire Zscaler in $44 billion deal
summary: CrowdStrike is reported to be acquiring Zscaler for $44 billion. The deal would combine endpoint protection with zero-trust network security, pitched around controlling AI agents.

headline: OpenAI and Cisco release open-source Shirudo eBPF runtime for AI-agent exploit shielding
summary: OpenAI and Cisco launched Shirudo, an open-source Linux runtime that lets AI agents write dynamic eBPF controls. The aim is to shield systems from exploits while patches are tested and rolled out. This is a product announcement, not a threat.

headline: Vendor piece argues for runtime visibility to cut vulnerability noise in AI-era software delivery
summary: RapidFort argues that AI-driven development is making software supply chains more complex and flooding teams with low-risk vulnerability findings. It promotes runtime visibility, container hardening and automated remediation as the answer.

headline: Test finds Chinese open-weight AI models beat US closed models at vulnerability discovery
summary: In a vulnerability discovery benchmark, DeepSeek outperformed five closed-source American AI models. It also cost much less to run. The findings come from a single test.

headline: Cloudera launches digital sovereignty offering with Mistral open-weight models
summary: Cloudera has launched Cloudera for Digital Sovereignty, a solution and partner ecosystem for running governed data and private AI. It works across sovereign clouds, private data centers and air-gapped environments. The offering integrates Mistral open-weight models.

headline: Dutch commentary says companies still conceal or downplay data breaches
summary: A Security.NL item reports criticism that companies still try to hide or play down data breaches. The criticism says they put their own interests ahead of the people affected. The source gives few details.

headline: Google Cloud CISO discusses agentic AI security and the future SOC analyst role
summary: In an interview, Google Cloud's CISO argues that attacker automation is making human-led SOC workflows obsolete. He talks about how AI agents may reshape junior analyst roles, why espionage groups are hard to detect, and which questions boards should ask.

headline: Schneier essay links recent US outages to fragile, under-funded infrastructure rather than attacks
summary: Bruce Schneier argues that a week of failures at Microsoft, the FAA, banks, United Airlines and the NSA were unrelated and, as far as is known, not caused by cyberattacks. He attributes them to old, centralised and under-funded digital infrastructure.

headline: White House names a new acting US national cyber director and seeks Senate confirmation for Davies
summary: The White House has given an additional role as acting national cyber director to a US intelligence official. The source headline calls him the intelligence chief, and the article's link names Jay Clayton. Pentagon CIO Kirsten Davies had led the office on a temporary basis, and the administration now hopes the Senate will confirm her to the permanent post.

headline: Dutch union CNV survey: many employees want camera glasses banned in the workplace
summary: A survey by the Dutch union CNV found that many workers worry about colleagues wearing camera-equipped smart glasses at work, and many want them banned. The story is about workplace privacy and policy in the Netherlands. No security incident is reported.

headline: SANS ISC flags ongoing scanning from Romanian VPS subnet 109.160.32.0/24 (AS198364)
summary: SANS ISC reports scanning activity seen by DShield sensors over the past 90 days from 109.160.32.0/24. The subnet belongs to a Romanian hosting and VPS provider, and the activity was still ongoing at the time of writing. The source does not say which services or vulnerabilities are being targeted.

headline: Dutch police seek victims of dozens of fake webshops; at least €47,000 stolen
summary: Dutch police are looking for people who were defrauded earlier this year through dozens of fake webshops. Police believe there are probably hundreds of victims and at least €47,000 in losses.

headline: Researcher's framework links ransomware aliases spanning a decade to real actors
summary: Dark Reading profiles a researcher who built a framework for tracing ransomware operators across a decade of aliases. The framework is presented as a way for security teams to attribute attackers.

headline: Vendor article sets out SOC budget priorities for 2027
summary: This sponsored-style article from ANY.RUN argues that the biggest SOC budget problem is lost analyst time. It cites the vendor's own estimate that faster threat analysis could recover 450 analyst hours per 1,000 alerts.

headline: UK court sentences Lapsus$ member behind GTA 6 leak to seven years, released on licence
summary: City of London Police announced that Arion Kurtaj, a Lapsus$ member who leaked Grand Theft Auto VI footage, was sentenced to seven years. He had pleaded guilty to six charges, including fraud and computer misuse offences. Because of time already served, he was released on licence the same day.

headline: CVE-2026-129975: double free in status line read code listed by Amazon Linux
summary: Amazon Linux Security Center lists CVE-2026-129975, a double-free bug in status line read code. The record doesn't name the affected component and doesn't confirm whether Amazon Linux is affected or whether a patch exists.

headline: Dutch court jails two fraud suspects caught with a decoy elderly man
summary: Two men from Rotterdam and Ridderkerk were sentenced to prison for fraud committed together. Police arrested them in an operation that used a decoy elderly man, which suggests a scheme targeting older victims.

headline: UK court sentences Rockstar Games/GTA VI hacker to seven years; released on licence for time served
summary: A British court sentenced the cybercriminal who hacked Rockstar Games and leaked Grand Theft Auto VI footage to seven years in prison. Because of time already served, he was released on licence the same day.

headline: Anthropic interviews at 58 companies examine how AI adoption is changing work and hiring
summary: Anthropic published research based on interviews with people at 58 companies that use Claude. Participants reported few layoffs but less hiring. They said AI delivered the most value when companies reorganized roles and workplaces around it. The study covers workforce effects, not security issues.

headline: Survey: Tor Browser users mainly seek to avoid ISP surveillance
summary: A report says the main reason people use Tor Browser is to get around monitoring by their internet service provider. The item is about user motivation and privacy, and it describes no vulnerability or incident.

headline: Ladybird browser ships first alpha after heavy use of AI coding agents
summary: The independent Ladybird browser has published its first alpha for macOS and Linux. The project says AI coding agents drove large gains in web-platform test pass rates. Its developers make no security promises at this stage, and the author advises against using it for sensitive accounts.

headline: Z.ai releases GLM-5.4 coding model with loop transformer architecture
summary: Z.ai has released GLM-5.4, its first model built on a looped transformer design. For now it is available only through the company's coding plan API, not as open weights.

headline: Law enforcement from 11 countries disrupts 57 illegal streaming services
summary: Police from 11 countries took down 57 illegal streaming services. The services ran hundreds of websites that drew more than 7.3 million visits a year. The source does not list the specific countries involved.

headline: SANS ISC Stormcast podcast for November 17, 2026
summary: SANS ISC published its daily Stormcast podcast episode. The source gives no content details.

headline: Datasette Agent 0.7a1 release improves side-panel navigation using URL fragment hashes
summary: Version 0.7a1 of the Datasette Agent plugin improves how chat-opened iframe side panels navigate, using URL fragment hashes so it works better with other plugins. This is a minor alpha feature release with no security content.

headline: Datasette-charts plugin released with automatic chart suggestions and Datasette Agent integration
summary: The new datasette-charts plugin suggests and builds charts from full query results using aggregating SQL, and it saves chart state in the URL fragment. Version 0.2a0 lets Datasette Agent create charts from chat requests. These are alpha feature releases with no security content.
